$comment: Known-unsupported manifest for the Treaty Node.js conformance harness.
Each entry names a corpus test (by case name = the .js file stem) or a glob over case names
that the Treaty runtime CANNOT yet pass, paired with the reason. The runner consults this file
for every corpus case and records a SKIP (with the reason below) WITHOUT evaluating the test --
the same outcome as an in-file `// CONFORMANCE: skip` directive, but tracked centrally so every
known gap is visible and diffable in one place (the way Bun/Deno track Node-compat gaps).
Glob metacharacters in `pattern`: `*` = any run of chars (incl. none), `?` = exactly one char;
everything else is literal and the whole case name must match. First matching entry wins, so a
specific entry may precede a broad glob to override its reason.
To re-enable a test once the runtime supports it: delete its entry here (and, if it had an
in-file skip directive, remove that too). See README.md.

unsupported.reason: node:https pending (no TLS transport; plain node:http loopback IS supported)
worker_threads is pending (no thread/MessageChannel support yet)
node:v8 introspection not exposed by the runtime
node:assert module is not implemented (tests use an inline assert helper instead)
native ESM import() of node: builtins inside a test is pending
node:repl is out of scope for the harness
node:inspector is out of scope for the harness
